info.title: wickwatch API
info.description:
REST API of wickwatch.

**Authentication:** log in with `POST /api/v1/auth/login` (password and TOTP code); the server sets the
`ww_session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict). All other endpoints except `/healthz` and
`/api/v1/auth/*` need it, or an API token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (admins create tokens in the web
app under *API tokens*). A token acts as the user who created it, with at most the token's role; it does not reach
`/api/v1/auth/*` or the token endpoints. Viewers may call GET endpoints only; state changes need the `admin` role.
State-changing requests with an `Origin` header from another site are rejected.

**MCP:** `POST /mcp` is a read-only Model Context Protocol endpoint (Streamable HTTP, stateless) for AI clients;
it takes an API token only.

**Errors** are JSON `{ "error": "<code>" }`. Codes of the broker/runtime adapters: `auth_failed`,
`not_found`, `unsupported`, `invalid_input`, `timeout`, `unavailable`. Others: `unauthenticated`,
`forbidden`, `forbidden_origin`, `rate_limited`, `internal` and endpoint-specific codes.

**Time** values are ISO 8601 in UTC; money is in the account currency.

get.summary: Health check
Who is logged in, and whether setup is needed

post.summary: First run: check the setup token and get a TOTP secret for the admin (2FA is optional)
First run: create the admin account and log in
post.description: Without `code` the admin is created without 2FA; with it, the code must match the secret from /setup/totp.

post.summary: Log in with password, plus TOTP code if 2FA is enabled
post.description: Wrong user name, password or code: 401 `invalid_credentials`. Right password but 2FA enabled and no `code`: 401 `totp_required`. With `remember` the session lasts 30 days and its cookie outlives the browser; without it the session ends with the browser, after 12 hours without a request, or after 7 days.

post.summary: End the session

get.summary: The logged-in user's sessions that are still valid, newest first

delete.summary: Log out the user's other sessions; this one stays
Log out one of the user's sessions, e.g. on a lost device
delete.description: Only the user's own sessions; any other id answers 404. Ending this session logs out like /logout.

post.summary: Start enabling 2FA for the logged-in user: get a new TOTP secret
Finish enabling 2FA with a code for the secret from /totp/setup
Change the password of the logged-in user; needs the current one
post.description: Other sessions of the user are logged out; this one stays. API tokens stay valid unless `deleteApiTokens` is true: then the user's tokens are deleted too, e.g. when the password may have leaked.

post.summary: Turn 2FA off for the logged-in user; needs the password and a current code
post.description: Wrong password: 403 `invalid_password`. Wrong or already used code: 401 `invalid_credentials`, as at login.

get.summary: Version, adapters and capabilities
Accounts, instances and alerts for the overview screen
One account: summary, instances, and all open positions and pending orders with their instance
CPU, memory, disk and time sync of the host
Instance detail: status, positions, orders, deals and key figures of the range

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: Everything since the instance's first trade; `days` is then ignored.

get.summary: Live log as Server-Sent Events
get.description: Sends the last `tail` lines (with LOG_ARCHIVE also those of replaced containers), then new lines as they appear. Each event is `event: log` with a LogLine as JSON; comment lines keep the connection open. Stream errors arrive as `event: error` with `{ error }`.

get.summary: The log as a text file
get.description: One line per log line: the UTC time, then the text as the instance wrote it. `period` limits it to the last 24 hours or 7 days; `all` is everything the runtime still has, with LOG_ARCHIVE also the kept logs of replaced containers. Streamed, so a long log never sits in memory.

get.summary: Search the whole log
get.description: Lines containing `q` (case ignored) that the filter keeps, newest 1000 at most, oldest first. `period` limits it to the last 24 hours (default) or 7 days; `all` is everything the runtime still has, with LOG_ARCHIVE also the kept logs of replaced containers.

post.summary: Start, stop or restart an instance

get.summary: Stored broker logins (without secrets)
get.description: Logins used only by accounts of another broker adapter (e.g. the demo data) are left out, like those accounts.

post.summary: Store a broker login; the secret is encrypted with MASTER_KEY

patch.summary: Change label, login or secret of a stored login (e.g. after a password change)

delete.summary: Delete a stored login that no account uses

get.summary: Accounts the broker offers for this login, and whether they are added already
Configured accounts of the active broker adapter

post.summary: Add an account; it is looked up at the broker with the given credentials

patch.summary: Rename an account or switch it to another stored login

delete.summary: Remove an account from wickwatch (nothing changes at the broker)

get.summary: Symbols the broker offers on the account (cached for an hour)
The account's deals of the last days, each with the instance it belongs to
get.description: Also the deals of no instance (manual trades, unclear ones), which no instance page shows. Asks the broker, so it is loaded when needed and not with every poll.

get.summary: Changes wickwatch noticed on a position (stop loss, take profit, volume, entry), oldest first
get.description: Also for a closed position. The broker is not asked: wickwatch compares the values of each load, so `at` is when a change was noticed and changes from before it first saw the position are missing.

post.summary: Close one open position at the broker
post.description: Destructive. `confirm` must repeat the position id.

post.summary: Cancel one pending order at the broker
post.description: Destructive. `confirm` must repeat the order id.

put.summary: Attribute a position (and its deals) by hand
put.description: `instance: null` means the position belongs to no instance, e.g. a manual trade.

delete.summary: Remove a manual attribution; the rules decide again

post.summary: Stop all instances of the account, cancel pending orders and close all positions
post.description: Destructive. `confirm` must repeat the account number.

get.summary: Challenge templates from templates/challenges/*.json
The account's challenge profile

put.summary: Set or replace the account's challenge profile

get.summary: Uploaded algo versions

post.summary: Upload an algo file (body: the file, application/octet-stream)
post.description: The name comes from the algo's metadata. `version` defaults to the bot's BotVersion parameter, else its build time.

post.summary: Read a parameter file (e.g. .cbotset) for this algo (body: the file, application/octet-stream)
post.description: Stores nothing. Values come converted to the algo's parameter types; `issues`, `unknown` and `missing` tell what did not fit.

delete.summary: Delete an algo version and its file (not while an instance uses it)

get.summary: Settings of the algos, by name; algos without any are left out

put.summary: Change the settings of an algo, for all its versions
put.description: `accountSizeParameter` names the parameter holding the account size the algo calculates with; wickwatch warns when it is far off the account's. `riskParameter` names the one holding the risk per trade in percent; wickwatch shows it in money and against the challenge's loss limits. Both must be number parameters of the newest version; fields left out stay as they are, null switches one off.

get.summary: Parameter templates, by algo and name
get.description: Values only for admins, as with configurations: they may hold licence keys.

post.summary: Save parameter values as a template, e.g. from a configuration version or a parameter file
post.description: The values are not checked against a version of the algo; applying the template does that.

get.summary: One parameter template
get.description: Values only for admins, as in the list.

patch.summary: Rename a parameter template or replace its values

delete.summary: Delete a parameter template; configurations saved from it stay as they are

get.summary: Audit log entries, newest first (admins)
get.description: `action` filters by exact action or, ending in a dot, by prefix (`instance.`); `target` by part of the target; `since` by time. `before` pages back: pass the smallest `id` of the previous page.

get.summary: API tokens, newest first (admins, with a session)

post.summary: Create an API token; the answer holds the token, which is not shown again
post.description: Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A request with it acts as the creating user, with at most the token's role. Without `expiresInDays` it does not expire. Needs the user's password and, with 2FA on, a current code, so a session left open cannot mint lasting access: wrong password 403 `invalid_password`, missing code 401 `totp_required`, wrong or used code 401 `invalid_credentials`. With API_TOKENS_REQUIRE_2FA=on a user without 2FA gets 403 `totp_needed`.

delete.summary: Delete an API token; requests with it fail from now on

get.summary: Schedules with the instances that use them and their current or next pause

post.summary: Create a schedule

get.summary: The names of the instances a schedule can pause: those set up in wickwatch

post.summary: The pauses of the next 14 days that rules would make, before they are saved
post.description: News pauses only with the events of the calendar fetched so far (NEWS_CALENDAR_URL).

put.summary: Change a schedule; its instances follow at the next check

delete.description: Its instances keep running without one; instances it paused are started at the next check.

get.summary: Instances set up in wickwatch, with their current configuration
get.description: Parameter values only for admins, as with the parameter file: they may hold licence keys.

post.summary: Set up an instance (saved only; nothing is started)

get.summary: A configuration version as a parameter file (e.g. .cbotset), to open it in the platform
get.description: Admins only: parameter sets may hold licence keys. `version` defaults to the current one. The body is the file.

get.summary: One managed instance with all configuration versions
get.description: Parameter values only for admins, as with the parameter file: they may hold licence keys.

delete.summary: Delete a managed instance, its container (stopping it) and its configuration history

post.summary: Save a new configuration version (also used to roll back to an old one)
post.description: Nothing is restarted; a running instance keeps its configuration until it is redeployed.

post.summary: Create or replace the instance with its current configuration
post.description: Replacing keeps a running instance running with the new configuration (a restart). `start` also starts a stopped one.

put.summary: Choose the schedules that pause an instance; it is paused while any of them pauses
put.description: The scheduler applies them within half a minute: during one of their pauses a running instance is paused at once. Without any, an instance they paused is started again.

tags.name: schedules
tags.description: Pauses on weekends, holidays and around news
